dedupe_keys.name: global field size map and crowdsourced field size data iiasa geo wiki 2017 campaign

description: A global map of agricultural field sizes built from crowdsourced interpretation of imagery. The Zenodo record says a Geo-Wiki campaign in June 2017 asked participants to interpret very high resolution imagery from Google Maps and Bing, collecting field size data for 130,000 unique locations, from which the authors produced an improved global field size map and estimated shares of very small to very large fields at global, continental and national levels, finding that smallholder fields occupy no more than 40 per cent of agricultural areas. The map and the crowdsourced data are a free download (40.7 MB zip) under CC BY 4.0, published 22 November 2018. Coverage is global agricultural land. Caveats: classes come from visual interpretation and vary by image quality. For simulation it separates smallholder from large-farm areas, which differ in how drought and floods hit production and recovery. A related catalogue record is the Geo-Wiki crowdsourced cropland reference data.
